routes.name: Permanencia Transitoria (tourist and business visit)
routes.summary: Tourists and business visitors can stay up to 90 days, extendable once by up to 90 more. Some nationalities need a consular visa or prior authorization first. Check the official list for your passport.

other: Must show enough money for the stay
No paid work, except specific one-off activities authorized by SERMIG (conferences, sports, shows, expert technical advice)
Which passports are visa-free was not confirmed here. Use the official nationality checker.
Stay cannot go past passport validity

stay.note: One extension of up to 90 days

sources.label: Consulado de Chile: visa information by nationality

routes.name: Tourist or business visa / prior consular authorization
routes.summary: Citizens of certain countries must get a visa or prior authorization from a Chilean consulate before arriving. It allows up to 90 days, one or multiple entries, and can be extended 90 days in Chile.

other: Only for nationalities on Chile's list. The list itself was not readable here, so check the consulate nationality tool.
Indian citizens need a sponsor letter from a company in India or Chile
No paid work, and generally no switching to residence inside Chile

steps: Check your nationality on the consulate visa page
Apply through the consular system (SAC) at a Chilean consulate

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Actividades remuneradas (work)
routes.summary: For people with an employment contract or accepted job offer in Chile, or a service contract of over 90 days. Apply from abroad.

other: Self-employed people only qualify with a prior contract with a Chilean or definitive resident for services over 90 days
Investors use a separate route

documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Work contract (employer signs before a Chilean notary, you sign before the consulate), or notarized job offer letter plus your signed acceptance
Employer tax folder, or proof of solvency to cover the contract

stay.note: Contract: up to 2 years, extendable 2 more. Job offer: 90-day permit, then 45 days after entry to file the contract, which gives a one-year extension.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Contract-based freelance work
routes.summary: Own-account workers can get temporary residence only with a prior service contract of over 90 days with a Chilean citizen or a definitive resident.

other: Service contract over 90 days with a Chilean or definitive resident
Not for investors

documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Service contract
Employer or contractor tax folder, or proof of solvency

sources.label: SERMIG: Residencia Temporal: Contract-based freelance work

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Trabajadores de temporada (seasonal)
routes.summary: For seasonal work with a contract. Up to 5 years in total, but no more than 6 months in Chile per calendar year.
documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Work contract (or notarized job offer for nationals of countries with bilateral agreements)
Employer solvency proof

sources.label: SERMIG: Residencia Temporal: Trabajadores de temporada (seasonal)

stay.note: Up to 5 years, extendable 2 more. Max 6 months per calendar year in Chile. File the notarized contract within 45 days of entry.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Jubilados y rentistas (retiree or passive income)
routes.summary: For retirees with a pension and people living on rental or financial asset income. Income must cover basic needs.

other: Income must cover at least basic needs, measured by Ministry of Social Development indicators. No fixed dollar amount is published on the page.

documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Retirees: pension certificate and last payment proof
Property rentiers: title certificate, lease, rent receipts
Financial asset rentiers: asset ownership certificate and income proof

sources.label: SERMIG: Residencia Temporal: Jubilados y rentistas (retiree or passive income)

stay.note: Duration not stated on the page. Extension needs proof of continued pension or income.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Inversionistas (investor)
routes.summary: For representatives or senior managers of a foreign company investing in producing goods or services in Chile. Needs an InvestChile sponsorship letter.

investment.note: Minimum, or equivalent in another currency

documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
InvestChile sponsorship letter
Document describing investment purpose, amount and your role

stay.note: Duration not stated. Extension needs proof of progress on the investment.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Gestión de negocios de múltiple entrada
routes.summary: For executives or managers who need to enter Chile repeatedly for business or investments held by companies in Chile. Total time in Chile max 6 months per calendar year.
documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Document explaining purpose of visits and business interests
Apostilled letter from the foreign institution you represent showing your role and related income

sources.label: SERMIG: Residencia Temporal: Gestión de negocios de múltiple entrada

stay.note: Max 6 months total per calendar year

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Estudiantes (study)
routes.summary: For people enrolled at a State-recognized school in Chile. You can work up to 30 hours a week. Apply from abroad.

other: Work limited to 30 hours per week without extra authorization

documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Certificate of regular student status or enrollment
Proof of financial support (bank deposits, transfers, sponsor sworn statement, or scholarship certificate)

stay.note: Duration not stated. Extension needs proof you still study and have funds.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Reunificación familiar (family)
routes.summary: For spouses or equivalent partners, parents, children under 18, children with disabilities, single children under 24 who study, and minors under the applicant's care, of a Chilean or definitive resident.

other: Sponsor must be a Chilean or a definitive resident

documents: Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Valid passport (from abroad) or ID (in Chile)
Proof of relationship (marriage, civil union, birth or custody certificate)
Notarized care and expenses declaration for dependents
Enrollment certificate for students; disability certification where relevant

stay.note: Duration not stated. Extension needs proof the relationship continues.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Razones humanitarias
routes.summary: For foreigners in Chile who are children, pregnant, or victims of trafficking, smuggling, or domestic or gender violence. Each case has its own requirements on SERMIG.

other: Requirements and duration vary by case and were not confirmed here

documents: Requirements differ per case. See the subpage for your situation.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Tratamiento médico
routes.summary: For people who need medical treatment in Chile from providers registered with the Superintendencia de Salud. Need a Chile address.
documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Medical certificate stating illness, treatment, duration and cost
Proof of funds for living costs and treatment (health insurance can cover treatment)

stay.note: Duration not stated. Extension needs proof treatment continues.

routes.name: Residencia Temporal: Religiosos
routes.summary: For members of a religious entity legally constituted in Chile under Law 19.638 who need to stay for reasons tied to their faith.
documents: Valid passport
Criminal record certificate
Photo
Certificate from your congregation
Registro Civil legal personality and board certificates
Favorable ONAR report

stay.note: Duration not stated on the page

routes.name: Working Holiday (Residencia Temporal, acuerdos internacionales)
routes.summary: Young people from partner countries can live and work in Chile for a limited time. Partners listed by SERMIG: Germany, Australia, Austria, Canada, Korea, Denmark, France, Hungary, Ireland, Iceland, Japan, Luxembourg, New Zealand, Poland, Portugal, Czech Republic, and the Pacific Alliance (Colombia, Mexico, Peru). Sweden is suspended.

other: Most agreements cover ages 18 to 30, but some are higher and some were extended recently. Check the MINREL page for your country.
Duration depends on each agreement and was not confirmed here
Apply from abroad. In the portal pick Tratados Internacionales, then Working Holiday.

documents: Passport valid at least one year (applying from abroad)
Criminal record certificate from home country or where you lived in the last 5 years (age 18+), issued within 60 days
Recent color photo, white background (JPG or PNG)
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized, translated if not Spanish or English, all as PDF
Proof of economic sufficiency
International health insurance
Anything extra the specific agreement requires

sources.label: SERMIG: Working Holiday (Residencia Temporal, acuerdos internacionales)
Consulado de Chile: Working Holiday requirements

routes.name: Mercosur and Bolivia reciprocity residence (Reciprocidad internacional)
routes.summary: Citizens of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay can get temporary residence up to 2 years under reciprocity. Paid work is allowed.

other: Fee depends on nationality. Bolivians pay no application fee.

documents: Valid passport (Bolivians may use a valid DNI)
Criminal record certificate for adults, within 60 days
Recent photo
Foreign documents apostilled or legalized
All as PDF

sources.label: SERMIG: Mercosur and Bolivia reciprocity residence (Reciprocidad internacional)

routes.name: Residencia Definitiva (permanent residence)
routes.summary: After 24 months of temporary residence you can apply, and in some cases 12 months. Absences add time. It can lapse if you are abroad over two years straight.

other: Generally 24 months of temporary residence (for applications after May 14, 2022)
Absences of 2 to 6 months mean 30 months, 6 to 12 months mean 36, over 12 months mean 48
12 months in some cases: family ties to Chileans or definitive residents, official missions, pensions or income, relevant investment
Can take longer for low income, unstable work, long absences or infractions
Apply before your temporary residence expires, no more than 90 days early

documents: Criminal record certificate (apostilled, under 60 days)
Passport ID page
Chilean foreigner ID card
Temporary residence stamp or visa
Photo
Proof of income or relationship as applicable

fees.label: General applicants
fees.note: Exempt: spouses of Chileans and minors

steps: Apply in the Portal de Trámites Digitales with ClaveUnica or your own account
Answer any document requests within 60 days
Book a Registro Civil appointment within 30 days of approval

routes.name: Carta de Nacionalización (naturalization)
routes.summary: Holders of definitive residence who have 5 years or more of residence since the electronic stamp can apply, from age 18. Must apply from inside Chile.

other: Valid definitive residence and 5 or more years of residence since the electronic stamp
Ages 14 to 17 can apply with parent or guardian notarized authorization
Dual nationality rules and any language test were not stated on the pages read

citizenship.note: Dual citizenship not confirmed on official pages read.

documents: Passport ID page, national ID or consular certificate
Criminal record certificate from country of origin
Photo
Proof of work activity and tax and debt certificates where relevant

routes.name: Carta de Nacionalización (spouse or relative of a Chilean)
routes.summary: Shorter route: 2 years of continuous residence since the electronic stamp, plus a tie to Chile such as 2 years married to a Chilean with a shared home, or a close Chilean relative.

other: Definitive resident with 2 years of continuous residence since the electronic stamp

Married to a Chilean for at least 2 years (marriage registered in Chile, living together), or blood relative to second degree of a Chilean or adopted by one, or child of a former Chilean who lost nationality before your birth

citizenship.note: Dual citizenship not confirmed on official pages read.

routes.name: Refugee status and asylum (Law 20.430)
routes.summary: Chile has a legal refugee process under Law 20.430, amended in 2024 by Law 21.655 to add an initial stage. See SERMIG for how to apply.

other: Procedure details were not read here
